thread:
support_lead: hi team — escalation from Acme. their p95/p99 on the tool router route spiked after our structured-output schema-validation rollout. they're seeing very long tails.
customer_acme: yep. started 2026-03-10 ~14:10 UTC for us. median OK but p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~780ms, p99 to ~1.5-2s. top offenders are calls to /v1/tool-run when we include tool schemas.
support_lead: can you paste a minimal repro and any traces?
customer_acme: repro curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tool-run \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: acme-req-42' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"find me articles","tools":[{"name":"search","schema":{...}},{"name":"summarize","schema":{...}},{"name":"kb","schema":{...}}]}'
```
customer_acme: sample trace lines from our agent: 
```
2026-03-10T14:11:02Z id=acme-req-42 route=/tool-run router.lat_ms=720 validate.sync_ms=540 model.total_ms=160
2026-03-10T14:11:06Z id=acme-req-88 route=/tool-run router.lat_ms=420 validate.sync_ms=200 model.total_ms=130
```
support_lead: looks like validate.sync_ms is consistently contributing a few hundred ms; router.lat_ms also elevated for some requests. eng_runtime, can you weigh in?
eng_runtime: initial read: validation landed as a synchronous stage that runs multiple JSON schema parses against candidate outputs. with N candidate tool selections and schema-per-tool, that multiplies work on the critical path. also our router does speculative expansion to evaluate top-3 candidates which increases N.
ml_infra: do we know whether it's the validation CPU cost, JSON parsing GC, or blocking on thread pool? any heap profiles?
customer_acme: our flamegraphs show CPU in a native JSON lib call, but we also see spikes in router queue depth when concurrency > ~40 connections. single-tool requests look fine.
ops_oncall: this was flagged by canary metrics post-rollout last week. we saw a bump in router queue latency on a handful of orgs.
eng_runtime: mitigation ideas: 
- quick toggle per-org to disable sync validation
- change flow to accept model output and run validation async, gate tool invocation with validated flag (deferred tool call)
- reduce router speculation (deterministic single-candidate routing for heavy customers)
- scale validation workers temporarily
- micro-opt of validator (switch to faster parser / compiled schema / incremental checks)

eng_runtime: fast patch we can do now: per-org config that flips `enable_schema_validation: false` for /tool-run. that removes the sync parse cost.
support_lead: customer asks they still want visibility when outputs don't match schema. can we still run validation async and emit metrics/alerts?
eng_runtime: yes — plan: disable sync validation but enqueue outputs into an async validator stream. async validator will validate and emit `schema_validation.failure` events and a sample of mismatches to logs.
ml_infra: note: async won't prevent tool misfires (i.e., invalid output causing downstream tool errors) if the tool is executed immediately. so we need to ensure when we disable sync validation we also don't call the tool synchronously in-case of schema mismatch. options: 
1) continue to call tool immediately (higher risk)
2) call tool only after async validation (adds latency again)
3) best-effort: call tool immediately but mark request with `validation_pending=true` and if async validator finds mismatch -> trigger compensating action (re-run or revert) and emit alert.
support_lead: customer prefers #3 for now — they want low latency but want us to surface mismatches quickly and ideally retry/compensate.
eng_runtime: OK — we can implement #3 quickly: flip sync validation off, enqueue for async validation, keep tool execution, but ship a `validation_status` event to their audit log. if async fails we send a webhook + increase a counter.
ops_oncall: we should set guardrails and rollback thresholds: 
- rollback if tool-error rate increases by >1.5x in 30m window
- rollback if async schema failure rate > 1% of validated outputs in 15m
- monitor p95/p99 latency improvements

eng_runtime: operational plan and canary: 
1) set per-org override for Acme: `enable_schema_validation=false`, `validation_mode=async`, `router_mode=single-candidate` with canary pct 5%
2) run for 1h, monitor: `route.tool-run.latency.p95`, `route.tool-run.latency.p99`, `tool.exec.errors`, `schema_validation.async.failures`, `router.queue_depth`
3) if stable, expand to 25% then 100%

eng_runtime: Console API payload for the quick canary: 
```
POST /api/console/v1/route-configs/acme-org
{
  "route":"/tool-run",
  "overrides":{
    "enable_schema_validation":"false",
    "validation_mode":"async",
    "router_mode":"single_candidate",
    "canary_pct":"5"
  }
}
```

deploy_bot: scheduled canary job created for acme-org at 2026-03-11T09:15Z (id=canary-215000)
support_lead: alex from support will coordinate with Acme and accept their test corpus. Acme, can you upload a small corpus (200 requests) for us to validate async pipeline against?
customer_acme: yes — uploading to pre-signed S3 now, link will be shared in 10m. we also want a flag so that when async validation fails, we get a sample of the response and stacktrace.
eng_runtime: we'll add a sample payload forward in the webhook and retain 7 days of mismatches. also create metric `schema_validation.async.sampled_failures` for alerts.
ml_infra: longer term: prioritize an incremental validator that validates token-by-token as model emits, and a router prefilter that uses cheap heuristics (e.g., token prefix checks / regex groups) to drop candidates before full schema parse. that should reduce worst-case cost from O(N*M) to O(K) where K << N*M.
eng_runtime: for immediate band-aid, we will also spin up one extra validation pool (x2) for the async queue for 24h.
ops_oncall: checklist before flip:
- create PD incident stub and runbook prefilled
- create dashboard widgets for the metrics above (p95/p99, tool errors, async failures)
- dry-run on staging with the Acme corpus
- set alert thresholds and escalation path

support_lead: timeline: canary tomorrow 09:15Z, watch for 1h, then decision. will update customer and keep them in the loop.
customer_acme: thanks — appreciate fast action. please share graphs when canary starts.
eng_runtime: assigning tasks: 
- eng_runtime: perform Console toggle and monitor canary (owner: eng_runtime)
- ml_infra: prototype incremental validator + prefilter POC (owner: ml_infra)
- ops_oncall: create incident + dashboards (owner: ops_oncall)
- support_lead: coordinate upload + comms (owner: support_lead)

support_lead: one more Q — is there any risk to data integrity if we keep calling tools immediately? any chance of side effects we can't undo?
ml_infra: depends on tool idempotency. we should ask Acme to mark side-effecting tools as `side_effect=true` in tool metadata and for those we should NOT execute until validation passes. that will be a policy change but doable as a short-term per-org rule.
customer_acme: we'll mark the few side-effecting endpoints. good catch.
support_lead: great. keeping thread open; will post canary start logs and the p95/p99 graphs.
eng_runtime: thanks all. we'll revert the sync validator to true if async failures or tool errors spike above thresholds.
ops_oncall: noted. PagerDuty will notify if thresholds hit.
support_lead: closing for now; will reopen when canary begins.
